Completion metadata and privacy

With GVISOR_CHECKPOINT_METADATA_ROOT unset, the helper returns without output. The screen sets it to the verified actual private DockerRootDir. At each of the four successful Checkpoint owner boundaries, after stopped timers and before cleanup or Restore, the helper walks metadata only: reject symlinks and non-regular entries, require nonempty regular files, cap traversal at 65536 entries, and reject logical bytes above2 GiB without integer overflow. It never opens checkpoint payloads. Write the typed six-field JSON exclusively as a 0600 per-container/checkpoint file under TEST_UNDECLARED_OUTPUTS_DIR, with canonical directories and validated names. There is no benchmark-stdout marker or payload copy.

The screen waits for the entire owned benchmark group to disappear, then reads only the exact bounded allowlisted metadata file with a privileged head command because the benchmark runs as root. Require the selected benchmark/checkpoint, exact filename/ID, fresh root-owned regular 0600 file, strict keys, positive bounded counts/bytes and completion-before-cleanup flag. Retain this JSON and its containerID for checkpoint-deletion verification even if polling missed the container. No other private output file or directory is read or archived.

The existing 200 ms observer still records task identities, disappearance races, disk availability and sampled logical bytes. Its sampled2 GiB/8 GiB stop thresholds remain active. It can miss a short-lived completed checkpoint, so it no longer requires a nonempty sample: the owning completion JSON must independently prove nonempty contents. Completion bytes are a point measurement, not peak bytes, allocated disk usage or a quota. Sampling and the new untimed stat/write work perturb whole-command costs. Canonical checkpoint/restore timer boundaries remain unchanged; new results are not paired with historical unhooked walltimes. Restore leaves retain their existing untimed two-second sleep.

Dependency isolation and rollback

Before changing packages retain original config bytes/mode/owner, service/socket state, original package archives and hashes, root/driver, full image references, volumes, namespaces and containerd version. Require no original containers and an identified supported service/socket. Never delete original images or choose an unrecorded endpoint. Use the existing newly owned 0700 private data-root/exec-root, unique absent namespaces and classic image backend. Validate the pinned daemon config and package identities before mutation. Any package-hook restart stays on this private store. The native Alpine namespace prerequisite must match the actual containerID/image/runc identity and clean its exact object.

Rollback first proves all owned stage/screen/setup groups absent, removes task containers and verifies retained checkpoint directories absent. Stop the daemon/socket and keep the prepared private config installed. Restore and verify original Docker packages and retained containerd BEFORE reattaching original config/store. After the package-hook daemon is stopped again, verify private config identity and original-plus-owned namespace inventory. Only task namespaces absent from the original inventory can be cleaned.

Before namespaced metadata deletion require zero containers/tasks/images, the exact native-proven empty snapshot/ingest headers, and valid unique lease IDs/content digests. Retain exact inventories. Delete only these namespaced lease IDs; relist content and require it to remain a subset of the original owned set. Delete remaining exact content refs, never global GC/prune/--sync. A nonzero content delete is accepted only if a bounded scoped relist proves that exact ref already absent and no unknown ref appeared; retain the original CLI status. Re-list all resource classes empty, remove the task namespace and require the original namespace set unchanged. Then restore original config/store, restart and verify versions, image references, volumes, root/driver, config identity and socket state. Unknown resources, ownership drift or unfinished restoration fail and retain the private configuration. The native 44386251141 probe proved these scoped 2.4.2 APIs on one rooted public 90-byte marker and one lease; that lease did not protect the marker and is not represented as doing so.
